title: Paninnis
description:
Panini’s are wonderful hot Italian sandwiches – but really just fancier versions of simple gilled cheese or grilled ham and cheese (and these basic ones can be so satisfying too).
The basic idea for the Panini version, of course, is: two slices of Italian bread stuffed with delicious goodies such as mozzarella, tomatoes, prosciutto, fresh basil, roasted red peppers, or whatever else makes you happy. Brush with extra virgin olive oil, then press between the hot plates of a panini grill for the best Italian style sandwich outside of Italy (maybe inside Italy too).
You can also make these in a pan on the stove top, but if you have a more elaborate stacked combination or any irregular shape, such as a cooked chicken breast, the panini grills work best.
The recipe here, a little unusual for a typical Panini, not to mention a bit cross-cultural, is for a Panini Cubano, with its distinctive dill pickle slices in the middle. This was actually the cover photo from the March 2009 Gourmet magazine.
Good taste is both high brow and low brow!
ingredients: 3 slices Swiss or other cheese garlic salt or powder olive oil or spray or melted butter
Spread one slice of bread with mustard and top with cheese, ham, pickles, and another slice of cheese,
directions: Spread the other slice of bread with mayonnaise, a little garlic salt or powder, cheese, and turkey, maybe another pinch of salt and pepper.
Put the two halves together and coat the outsides with a little olive oil, spray, or melted butter.
Put sandwich in the panini maker and cook until nicely browned and the cheese has melted (or the green light comes on).
If preparing on the stovetop, cook in a covered sauté pan for 3 to 4 minutes, until nicely browned, then flip, cover, and cook it for an additional 3-4 minutes.
After removing the sandwich from the grill, let it rest a moment before cutting.
